post_title: Updating Graphic Designs on Patterns through Source File Modification
post_details: I have a query regarding the updating process of clothing designs created in Illustrator. When I design a specific pattern or motif in Illustrator, I typically export it as a file and then import it onto the garment pattern I'm working on. Suppose that, after having integrated this design into my garment pattern, I realize I want to make a slight change to it. I then go back to Illustrator, make the necessary modifications, and re-export the updated file, ensuring it retains the same name and is saved in the exact location as the original file. My question is: Is it possible for the graphic that has already been imported onto the garment pattern to automatically update to reflect this change, given that the source file has been altered and saved again in the same spot with the same name? Thanks a lot

comments.comment_body: Hi 24539181088025 Yes you can do this in CLO. In order to do this you will need to make sure that the graphic is set up properly in Ai and placed properly on the art board. Then Instead of applying the graphic as a PNG or JPEG you apply the actual Ai file. Then if you make changes you can refresh the texture by R-clicking in the 3D background and selecting Refresh Textures (short cut F5).

Hi CLO Designers I made some test with saving obj as avatar first, and then converting obj-avatar to CLO-avatar. Unfortunately the result is not much different form how it was before:

Hi 427744626854 Errors like this can occur when the mesh mesh is not ideal from the original export. The Webbing that is happening under the arms and between the legs is most likely from the mesh being joined there originally. So CLO will not know there needs to be spacing. You may want to edit the OBJ mesh and shaping in a program like Blender (it is free) before bringing it into CLO.

Hi CLO Thank you for a good advice! Yes, agree, if original obj pose is not exact A or T it will most likely give some webbing and twisting in ankle and wrist. But A pose is challenging for plus sizes cause under arm and between legs will be joined. Therefore we scan with leg more spread out and arms more rounded up. I'm just wondering, why the result after converting is always better on Skin_Style and Rigging_Only and the worst in Size_Editable since original obj is the same? Meaning, mesh issue should be the same for all 3 avatars? So if CLO knows spacing for the first 2 avatars then it should know for 3rd? But somehow Size_Editable is mostly loosing the original body shape and get webbings (and twist in wrist/ankle)?

Besides, I have tried to cut up the body at the place where it was joined using the scanning program: There is a space between arm and body but when I move the arm, body is being pulled up instead of getting more space at armhole: Any good advice how to solve this? Thank you in advance !!!

Hi. So the largest issue is most likely from the avatars arms not being in the correct position to start. The Arms should NOT be rounded which is why the wrist and forearm look warped later on. If you are able to rescan the model with the arms in a straight T or A pose this will help. So that there will be plenty of spade under the arms For the legs we do understand that with a larger size you may not be able to have the model stand feet together. This is where you may need to adjust the mesh in another program before bringing into CLO. Otherwise we may recommend looking at the ASTM plus sizes that come with CLO and see if you can edit the size from the preset to better match your models measurements

post_details: Hello, I have a problem with this round collar on a t-shirt. I can't make it flat. The collar is a band that measures 82% of the perimeter (41,18cm for a 50,22cm 2D line length). Despite this, the collar remains chimney-shaped. What can I do? I have the impression that my avatar's neck is preventing the collar from lying flat.

comments.comment_body: Hi 10733584378265 There are a few things that can help here. 1 - Have you Turned on Folder Rendering for the Internal Line where the neckband is folded over? This will increase the sharpness of the fold 2 - Have you reduce the Skin offset on the Avatar? It is like a force field that protects the avatar from the garment while building. The default is 3mm, but you can always adjust in the Avatar Property Editor. post_title: outer sinks in inner top on rendering / 렌더링 시 아우터가 이너에 묻혀버림
post_details: 안녕하세요 제목 그대로입니다. 고품질 3d 렌더링 시에도 멀쩡히 나오는데 렌더링 화면에서는 하단 사진처럼 옷이 묻혀버려요 ㅠㅠ 무슨 문제인지 아시는 분 답변 부탁드립니다.. - hi, as the uploaded picture below, my outer literally sinks in the inner. even it works well on high quality 3d render but happens only on rendering and i have no idea what's wrong. please give me answer if someone knows how to do..

comments.comment_body: Hi 20553125598745 It looks like your under layer has Additional Thickness Rendering applied or possibly Fur (hard to tell as the image is blurry). This means that your vest is not actually sinking into the dress, but the dress is popping out. For Fur as it is only added in the Render engine it is visual and does not have any physics. So it will pop through other pattern pieces layered over it. One Solve is to remove the fur from the pattern pieces underneath that the vest sits over so it will not pop out. Another is to use Fur base maps which will remove fur from specific areas. We have a video HERE on our youtube We hope this helps!
i just solved this problem thanks to your answer. really appreciate you!
Wonderful! Thank you for letting us know :)
